title: Walk in His ways (Sotah 14a)
hookLine: God clothed the naked, visited the sick, comforted mourners, buried the dead: so should we
tomorrow: who else was asked before Israel said yes?

lines: AFTER THE LORD SHALL YE WALK.
cards: Follow is a button now. Tap it, and someone's day scrolls past yours. The Torah has its own follow command: "After the LORD your God shall ye walk."
And the Talmud spots a problem right away. The same Torah calls God "a devouring fire." How do you walk behind a fire?
Get close and you're gone. Stay far away and you're not following anyone. In tractate Sotah, Rabbi Hama son of Rabbi Hanina asks it out loud: what can it mean to follow God?

teach.b: His answer: follow God's ways, not God's footsteps. Then he proves each one from the Torah's own stories. God clothed the naked: Adam and Eve leave the garden in garments God made.
So you clothe the naked. God visited the sick: after Abraham's circumcision, God appears to him by the trees of Mamre. So you visit the sick, bikur cholim.
God comforted mourners: after Abraham dies, God blesses Isaac his son. So you comfort mourners. God buried the dead: the Talmud reads the verse at the end of Deuteronomy as God burying Moses.
So you bury the dead. There's the puzzle, solved. Nobody can trace a fire's footprints.
But the Torah left a trail shaped like errands: a coat, a hospital visit, an hour at a shiva house, a shovel at a grave.

Read them in order and they trace a whole life: a body dressed, a body sick, a family grieving, a body laid to rest. Every one is a way of showing up. None asks for the perfect words, and none comes with a guest list.
In the same passage, Rabbi Simlai adds the line people quote: the Torah begins with kindness and ends with kindness.
Clothes in the first pages, a burial on the last. Yesterday was who to be like. Today is what to do on Thursday.

how: Jewish communities organize these four as everyday duties: bikur cholim groups visit the sick, people bring meals and sit with mourners during shiva, and a chevra kadisha cares for the dead before burial.

games.q: what does “walk in his ways” mean?
o: follow God by keeping each rule of the law exactly
follow God by staying near the Temple and its priests
follow God by doing what God did: clothe, visit, comfort

games.q: God did it first — tap the pairs.
p: Moses, at the end of Deuteronomy

s: the Talmud reads 'walk after God' as a call to follow God's footsteps
God is a devouring fire. Rabbi Hama says: follow God's ways instead.
each of the four acts is proved from a story in the Torah
garments in Eden, Abraham at Mamre, Isaac blessed, Moses buried.
visiting the sick is meant for family and close friends
none of the four comes with a guest list.

games.q: a classmate's dad died. you're not close, and the family is sitting shiva this week. you're scared you'll say the wrong thing. what's the move?
o: stay away; mourners want only close family around them right now.
go, sit a while, and let your being there do most of the talking.
write a long note about what Jewish texts teach on death and grief.
games.why: God comforted Isaac, so you comfort mourners. the four ways are ways of showing up; none of them asks for perfect words.

practice: Pick one of the four, and let a face come to mind: someone who's sick, someone grieving, someone who needs something practical.
Write them a short message now, presence rather than advice, something like thinking of you, can I bring dinner this week. Send it, or keep it ready for when the time is right.

wordCard.voice: Walk in His ways: Rabbi Hama's answer to following a God who is a fire. Clothe, visit, comfort, bury, because God did it first.

orig.note: Hebrew: visiting the sick, one of the four ways God walked first.

carryVoice: Keep this one: walk in his ways. The trail starts with a coat and ends with a shovel, and it's kindness all the way.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Sotah 14a (Rabbi Hama son of Rabbi Hanina: walk after God's attributes; the four acts; Rabbi Simlai: the Torah begins and ends with kindness)

sources.q: After the LORD your God shall ye walk
